legacy_root.title: Extract scoring rules and extremizing methods from forecasting tournaments
legacy_root.question: Which proper scoring rules and aggregation adjustments (extremizing, recency weighting, team-versus-individual effects) are validated by forecasting-tournament research, and which can score a council's confidence trajectory with the data a council actually produces?
legacy_root.answer: Strictly proper scores validated for tournament use are Brier (primary; two-component 0–2), log, and spherical (robustness). Extremizing the crowd mean with t(p)=p^a/(p^a+(1-p)^a) improved Brier from 0.187 to 0.148 on Baron Table 1 high-expertise means (a=2.43 vs a=1). Recency as part of Atanasov's decay+weight+extremize bundle cut 0.027 Brier versus the 0.214 market baseline (13%, t(113)=2.69). Isolated recency and the Satopää logit magnitude are E3 and are not recommended. Team elicitation beat independent last-week Brier 0.16 vs 0.26 (Mellers Table 1 Year 2). A council confidence trajectory is scoreable only when each point is a probability on a claim that later resolves against a named source; normative design recommendations without a named observable are the unscoreable control. SUCCESS:RES-0083

unscoreable_output_type.why_unscoreable: A strictly proper score is a function of a predictive distribution and a realized outcome ω. A council sentence of the form 'the program SHOULD bind the rules root to the repository path' does not name an ω independent of the later operator decision. If the operator later adopts the advice, that is a choice, not a resolving event. No Brier, log, or spherical number is defined. Atanasov/Mellers/Baron all score questions that IARPA resolved on the calendar; they do not score advice.

council_applicability.can_score_confidence_trajectory: Yes, with Brier (primary) and log (secondary), iff each trajectory point is a probability — or a band mapped by a published table — on a claim that later resolves CONFIRMED or REFUTED against a named settling_probe and horizon.
council_applicability.extremizing: Apply only after aggregating ≥2 probability reports. Do not extremize a single agent's self-confidence path and call it GJP-validated.
council_applicability.recency: Apply only when the same claim is updated over time. Use the bundle (recency + performance weights + extremizing), not the E3 isolated row.
council_applicability.team_effect: Not a scoring rule. Do not treat 'run a team council' as a proper score. Human GJP teams beat isolates; LLM-council transfer is out of scope.
council_applicability.band_mapping_is_convention: Mapping almost-certain/likely/roughly-even/unlikely/remote onto numbers is a local convention. GJP did not validate a Kent table. Whatever map is used must be published next to the scores.

title: Extract scoring rules and extremizing methods from forecasting tournaments
question: Which proper scoring rules and aggregation adjustments (extremizing, recency weighting, team-versus-individual effects) are validated by forecasting-tournament research, and which can score a council's confidence trajectory with the data a council actually produces?
answer: Strictly proper scores validated for tournament use are Brier (primary; two-component 0–2), log, and spherical (robustness). Extremizing the crowd mean with t(p)=p^a/(p^a+(1-p)^a) improved Brier from 0.187 to 0.148 on Baron Table 1 high-expertise means (a=2.43 vs a=1). Recency as part of Atanasov's decay+weight+extremize bundle cut 0.027 Brier versus the 0.214 market baseline (13%, t(113)=2.69). Isolated recency and the Satopää logit magnitude are E3 and are not recommended. Team elicitation beat independent last-week Brier 0.16 vs 0.26 (Mellers Table 1 Year 2). A council confidence trajectory is scoreable only when each point is a probability on a claim that later resolves against a named source; normative design recommendations without a named observable are the unscoreable control. SUCCESS:RES-0083
